alt.en: A narrow column of heavy black-letter type inside a ruled frame, verses 22 to 27 of a Bible chapter, beginning "22 And the LORD spake vnto Moses, saying," and including "24 The LORD blesse thee, and keepe thee: 25 The LORD make his face shine vpon thee, and be gracious vnto thee: 26 The LORD lift vp his countenance vpon thee, and giue thee peace." It ends "and I will blesse them."
alt.es: Una columna estrecha de letra gótica gruesa dentro de un marco de líneas, con los versículos 22 a 27 de un capítulo de la Biblia, que empieza "22 And the LORD spake vnto Moses, saying," e incluye "24 The LORD blesse thee, and keepe thee: 25 The LORD make his face shine vpon thee, and be gracious vnto thee: 26 The LORD lift vp his countenance vpon thee, and giue thee peace." Termina "and I will blesse them."

caption.en: Numbers 6:22 to 27 in the King James Bible of 1611: the priestly blessing in the wording that Lutkin set nearly three hundred years later, "The LORD blesse thee, and keepe thee".
caption.es: Números 6:22 a 27 en la Biblia King James de 1611: la bendición sacerdotal en la redacción que Lutkin puso en música casi trescientos años después, "The LORD blesse thee, and keepe thee" ("Jehová te bendiga, y te guarde").

source: The Holy Bible, Conteyning the Old Testament and the New (London, 1611), Numbers 6:22 to 27 (cropped to that column), from the Early English Books 1475-1640 microfilm
library: Internet Archive (scan of the Early English Books 1475-1640 microfilm)
callNumber: Internet Archive bim_early-english-books-1475-1640_the-holy-bible-conteyni_bible-english_1611_0, image n230; microfilm canister IA40313703-03
licenceEvidence: Printed London 1611; the King James translators all died in the 1600s. A microfilm and its scan are faithful copies of a flat page and add no new copyright (see rights.md).
credit: Internet Archive, from the Early English Books 1475-1640 microfilm

alt.en: A page of printed choral music numbered 4: two systems, each with four voice staves over a two-stave organ part, the words "A - men" repeated under every voice, with the markings mp, cresc., f, dim., poco a poco e rit. and pp, and fermatas on the last chord. A footnote reads "NOTE: If it is desired to use the Sevenfold Amen separately, the Bass is to begin with the half note." and below it "C. F. S. Co. 524".
alt.es: Una página de música coral impresa con el número 4: dos sistemas, cada uno con cuatro pentagramas de voces sobre una parte de órgano de dos pentagramas, con las palabras "A - men" repetidas bajo cada voz, las indicaciones mp, cresc., f, dim., poco a poco e rit. y pp, y calderones en el último acorde. Una nota al pie dice "NOTE: If it is desired to use the Sevenfold Amen separately, the Bass is to begin with the half note." y debajo "C. F. S. Co. 524".

caption.en: The sevenfold Amen on page 4 of Summy's octavo, whose Chicago printing of 1900 is the earliest known, here in a later printing from the same plates, with the footnote that says the Amen may be sung on its own.
caption.es: El Amén séptuple en la página 4 de la partitura en octavo de Summy, cuya impresión de Chicago de 1900 es la primera conocida, aquí en una tirada posterior hecha con las mismas planchas, con la nota al pie que dice que el Amén puede cantarse por sí solo.

source: Peter C. Lutkin, The Lord Bless You and Keep You: Farewell Anthem with Sevenfold Amen (Chicago: Clayton F. Summy Co., copyright 1900, renewed 1928), a later Summy printing (cover no. 1089), p. 4, plate C. F. S. Co. 524
library: Internet Archive (community upload, Folkscanomy collection; no holding library named)
callNumber: Internet Archive TheLordBlessYouAndKeepYou_700, image n3; the same scan is IMSLP #525534
licenceEvidence: Published Chicago 1900; music by Peter C. Lutkin, died 1931, the song's own maker; nothing by anyone else on the page. Page 2 of the same copy: "Copyright 1900 by Clayton F. Summy Co. / Copyright renewed 1928 by Peter C. Lutkin". The uploader's Public Domain Mark tag is not relied on. Faithful scan of a flat page (see rights.md).

alt.en: A cream hymnal page headed "Chants and Occasional Pieces" in Gothic letters, then "748 THE LORD BLESS YOU AND KEEP YOU" and "PETER C. LUTKIN", marked "Smoothly and deliberately". Four systems of two staves carry the words from "The Lord bless you and keep you" to "gra-cious un-to you. A-MEN." At the foot: "Copyright, C. F. Summy Co. Used by permission" and the page number 532.
alt.es: Una página de himnario de color crema con el encabezado "Chants and Occasional Pieces" en letra gótica, y después "748 THE LORD BLESS YOU AND KEEP YOU" y "PETER C. LUTKIN", con la indicación "Smoothly and deliberately". Cuatro sistemas de dos pentagramas llevan la letra desde "The Lord bless you and keep you" hasta "gra-cious un-to you. A-MEN." Al pie: "Copyright, C. F. Summy Co. Used by permission" y el número de página 532.

caption.en: No. 748 in the Methodist Hymnal of 1905, of which Lutkin was one of the two music editors: his blessing on two staves, with a short two-bar Amen in place of the sevenfold one.
caption.es: El n.º 748 de The Methodist Hymnal de 1905, del que Lutkin fue uno de los dos editores musicales: su bendición en dos pentagramas, con un Amén breve de dos compases en lugar del séptuple.

source: The Methodist Hymnal: Official Hymnal of the Methodist Episcopal Church and the Methodist Episcopal Church, South (New York: Eaton & Mains; Cincinnati: Jennings & Graham, 1905), No. 748, "The Lord Bless You and Keep You", p. 532
